verdict.rationale: WezTerm's multiplexer keeps tabs alive. The docs say a connection to a remote wezterm instance "preserves your tabs", and a runtime probe shows a daemonized wezterm-mux-server holding windows, tabs and panes independently of the GUI. That lets a developer reattach after closing or losing the GUI, but nothing shows layouts or working directories surviving a restart of the mux server, a machine reboot or a crash. The OSC 7 working-directory feature only seeds the directory of newly spawned tabs; it does not restore them. Missing for 10: restoring sessions after a reboot or mux-server crash, persisting working directories across restarts, saving and loading layouts, and independent corroboration of session restore.
